R621.note: Allowlist of content types (plus a magic-byte alternative) correctly closes the metadata-trust gap without changing legitimate behavior.

R622.note: Removes the shell entirely and passes archiveName as a discrete exec argument; output unchanged for legitimate input.

R623.note: Adds an ownership check comparing the caller's account claim to the invoice's AccountId, the correct IDOR fix shape; assumes an account_id claim exists but that's a reasonable synthesis for this stub.

R624.note: escapeHtml4() on both fields closes the reflected XSS with no other observable change.

R625.note: random_bytes(32)+bin2hex replaces uniqid() and drops the attacker-influenced prefix entirely; correct and clean.

R626.note: Correct token-based CSRF shape, but the recommended csurf package has been deprecated/unmaintained by its author since 2022 in favor of alternatives, which the write-up doesn't flag.

R627.note: SqlParameter binding for the stored-proc call is the standard, correct fix.

R628.note: Content sniffing + random filename + path containment closes both traversal and type-trust issues; explicitly discloses the read-path filename coupling. Minor: comment claims O_EXCL but os.WriteFile doesn't set it (negligible given random 16-byte names).

R629.note: Argument-list exec with shell=False closes the injection while preserving the conversion behavior.

R630.note: std::string::at() converts the OOB write into a bounds-checked exception, the standard fix for this sink; no catch is added at the call site but that's an acceptable fail-fast tradeoff, noted as intended.

R631.note: Null-checks both call sites of the nullable Long; isDiscountApplied fix also closes a second latent NPE without changing non-null semantics.

R632.note: markupsafe.escape() applied to all three interpolated values closes the XSS cleanly.

R633.note: Normalizes destination once up front and compares against the normalized form consistently, correctly fixing the inconsistent-normalization bypass.

R634.note: Blacklisting sys.modules entries and restricting __builtins__ doesn't touch IronPython's actual RCE surface (direct CLR/System.* access via `clr`), so the vector is not really closed despite the 'defense in depth' framing; legitimate math/string scripts still work fine though.

R635.note: Rejecting non-null scheme/host after URI parsing correctly restricts redirects to relative paths, including scheme-relative bypasses.

R636.note: Content sniffing, allowlist, and random filename correctly close both the type-trust and traversal issues; response now reports the generated name rather than the original, visible in the shown code.

R637.note: snprintf with sizeof(line) is the correct fix; truncation on overlong input is explicitly disclosed.

R638.note: Checks both getHost() and isAbsolute(), correctly rejecting scheme-relative and opaque-scheme (javascript:) redirects in addition to absolute URLs.

R639.note: Bound `?` parameter via DB::select() closes the injection with identical query semantics.

R640.note: Switching the cache to own std::string instead of a non-owning string_view is the correct fix for the dangling-view UAF; no external API changes.

R641.note: Reject + canonicalize + startsWith containment is the standard, complete path-traversal fix; error-response semantics preserved via try/catch.

R642.note: Parameterized JNDI search filter ({0} + filterArgs) is the correct LDAP-injection fix and compiles against the documented overload.

R643.note: SecureRandom-backed token replaces Math.random(); same variable feeds both cookie and session so comparison logic is unaffected by the format change.

R644.note: check_password() returns False for the legacy plaintext-stored passwords (not a recognized hash format), so swapping the comparison before running the migration script locks out every existing user; the write-up sequences the code change first and the migration second without flagging that this ordering causes a full outage.

R645.note: crypto/rand.Read() replaces math/rand/v2; modulo-bias on the alphabet index is minor and explicitly acknowledged.

R646.note: jwt.verify() with an explicit algorithms allowlist replaces jwt.decode(), correctly gating on signature validity.

R647.note: PreparedStatement with bound parameter is the standard SQL injection fix; behavior otherwise unchanged.

R648.note: Stripping CR/LF (or strconv.Quote alternative) closes the log-injection vector; required import addition is called out.

R649.note: Reorders the session write to after login_user(), matching the stated guidance exactly and preserving both operations' effects.

R650.note: Primary array-form exec() fix is correct, but the offered 'alternative' (`/bin/sh -c osCommand+data`) re-concatenates untrusted data into a shell string and reintroduces the identical injection, presented without any warning that it doesn't fix the vulnerability.

R651.note: Content-sniffing allowlist + UUID storage name correctly closes the vector, but the JSON response still returns the client-supplied safe_name while the file is actually stored under the generated UUID name -- the two silently diverge, undisclosed.

R652.note: os.path.realpath() on both sides resolves symlinks before the containment check, correctly closing the escape.

R653.note: mysql2 `?` placeholder with bound array argument is the correct parameterized-query fix.

R654.note: redis-py's hset() with RESP-encoded arguments replaces the raw inline-protocol string, correctly closing the CRLF command injection.

R655.note: database/sql `?` placeholders with bound args, correct order, standard Go SQL injection fix.

R656.note: Replacing hand-built SMTP protocol lines with Jakarta Mail's Transport/Session API and strict InternetAddress validation closes the CRLF command injection.

R657.note: Null-checks the shared_ptr returned by weak_ptr::lock() before dereferencing; discarding the notification on a dead connection is disclosed and expected.

R658.note: Whitelisting exact allowed sort/column strings is the correct fix for an ORDER BY clause that can't be parameterized; signature and control flow preserved.

R659.note: Correctly identifies that Roslyn scripting must be replaced or AST-whitelisted, but delivers no concrete, committed implementation -- only narrated options and a 'hypothetical' example -- so the vector isn't actually closed by what's handed over.

R660.note: htmlspecialchars() with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 and explicit UTF-8 correctly closes the reported sink.
